description: Requirement register for the skeleton-and-modules redesign (D22). Each requirement names the evidence tiers that close it: T1 mechanism tests, T2 wiring (a report from real runs), T3 agent-in-the-loop scenarios, T4 adversarial rounds. A closed requirement lists, per tier, repository files that exist and contain its id. Every requirement of a completed phase must be closed or deferred with a reason.

requirements.statement: Every governed record (steering, units, findings, decision log, module registry, approvals) lives inside the package and is committed with it; nothing load-bearing lives outside it.

STEERING.json holds the seven M2 answers (level, depth, emphasis, notation, example style, exclusions, tone), when they were recorded, per-chapter overrides and a change history; malformed steering is refused.

A unit record carries id, locator (section, ordinal, contentHash), form, role (teaching|framing), origin (one of the origin kinds or unknown), spineNodes, judgment kinds and evidence; malformed unit records are refused.

A finding carries module, kind, units, typed evidence, statusClass (defect|obligation|question), route (agent|digest|interrupt), recommendation, status and basis; blocksPublish is true exactly for defect and obligation.
A finding's id is content-addressed over module, kind, units and evidence, so the same finding on unchanged content always has the same id and a changed basis yields a new one.
The decision log is append-only JSONL with a gap-free sequence; a later log must extend the earlier one byte for byte.

Every log record carries the hash of its predecessor and its own hash, and the verifier reports any break in the chain (never throwing); the acceptance rule verifyAgainstCommitted checks the working log and that it extends the committed one.
Every log record names its party: role instructor, agent or harness, with a name (and a model id for an agent).

Log record types are enumerated (intake, transition, version, approval, glance-confirmation, steering, answer, confirmation, authorship-confirmation, revision, divergence, dispatch, unit-retirement, publish, module-change); unknown types are refused.
Log tampering is detected: an edited record, a deleted or reordered record, a forged record inserted mid-chain, a rewritten history that no longer extends the committed log.
The module registry lists each enabled module with its version and maturity (stable|trial|experimental) for this package; unknown maturity is refused.

Every module declares name, version, serves (Control|Confidence|Coherence), checkpoints (V0–V8), reads, emits (kind, evidence type, default route), mayBlock, method, cost, profiles and maturity; a module without a valid manifest is not run.
A module is a function from a package snapshot to findings; a deterministic module gives byte-identical findings on the same snapshot.
Modules only emit findings; they never write deliverables, the spine, steering or the log.
A defect is admitted only after the harness re-runs its evidence; evidence that is missing or fails the re-run turns it into a question (S1).
Trial findings are delivered as questions and never block; experimental modules are off unless enabled; stable findings keep their declared class.
A module runs only in the use profiles it declares (e.g. rights checks only in public packages).
Promotion trial → stable is a logged module-change decision that cites the module's study bar met on development cases.

Each run produces a wiring report: which modules ran at which checkpoint, which finding kinds were produced and routed, which record types were written and read; a registered module, finding kind or record type with no producer or no consumer on the fixtures is flagged.
The gate blocks publishing exactly when there is an open defect or obligation from a stable module or the skeleton core, an invalid approval, or a broken log chain; questions never block.
Every gate run verifies the decision log against the committed log (verifyAgainstCommitted); any failure is a blocking skeleton finding.

Every finding is routed agent, digest or interrupt; interrupt is used only for the four D14 reasons (unresolvable spine-scope conflict, missing input, rights blocker in a public package, a request that would change the spine).
The spine is the course concept map plus, per chapter, a concept map and an assessment guide; all three are parsed.
Every objective, concept, key term, misconception and assessment-guide entry carries a stable anchor; the harness mints one where missing; ids are never positional.
The assessment guide is parsed into anchored entries, at least one per objective, each with question types, cognitive level and count.

Spine well-formedness is checked deterministically before approval: required sections, unique anchors, objective↔guide entries, prerequisites resolve, no prerequisite cycles, chapter sequence matches the manifest; failures are defects routed to the agent.
Each spine item is marked instructor, standardized or proposed-by-agent, and the approval view shows the three differently.
Spine critique is raised only as questions, within the digest budget, and never blocks.
An approval record covers named spine documents at a content hash and version, names the instructor, time and note, and quotes the instructor's words.
There is one approval per chapter (concept map + assessment guide) and one for the course map; a course-map change voids only the chapters whose nodes or order it touches.
A covered document whose hash no longer matches voids its approval; a chapter without a valid approval cannot publish.

Re-approval has two weights: a light change (every node and anchor kept; no fact, value, name, number, negation, level, question type or count changed) needs a glance confirmation and the work loop continues; anything else is substantive (diff and impact preview; new content pauses); when unsure, substantive.
The approval view previews what will be built: objectives and, per objective, the number and kind of example and practice questions implied by the guide.
Steering is asked once (M2): seven questions with defaults inferred from the inputs, accept-all in one action, per-chapter overrides.

A structural change opens a new major version with lineage — of the chapter, of both chapters when an objective moves between them, or of the course when the chapter list or order changes — and the changed scope cannot be re-approved until it does.
A spine revision that keeps every surviving node's identity stays within the version and is re-approved (light: a glance; otherwise full), never forced into a new version.

The harness segments every deliverable into units (paragraph, list item, table row, equation, callout, figure, slide group, question, answer, a heading that prints, a printed orz-paged element); no prose is left out.
Unit ids survive rewording and reordering; splits and merges are recorded; an unmatched unit is new.
Every unit records its origin: source-derived, agent knowledge, computed, instructor-authored, found evidence, or unknown.
A change with no recorded agent write is an edit of unknown authorship: checked like agent text and raised once in the digest (accept as mine / name the author / revert).
A skeleton-owned deterministic classifier assigns judgment kinds, erring toward inclusion; a unit with several kinds is checked under each; the agent may add a kind, never remove one.
Framing units may not carry mechanical or semi-mechanical content and are still checked for off-spine content.
A semi-mechanical unit without an admitted evidence record is an open obligation (it claims nothing is wrong, and blocks publishing).
An objective or assessment-guide entry with no linked unit, and a unit with no spine link, are open obligations.
requirements.source: D19-A, D19-I; Control C1, C3, C5

requirements.statement: After a change, every affected unit not yet re-verified is an open obligation; nothing reaches a published snapshot stranded.
Units carried into a new major version enter it as open obligations (re-verify), never as verified.
The impact set of a change covers the mechanical dependency kinds (shared value, shared term, spine node, source, derivation) and declared prerequisites.
A meaning-preserving edit raises nothing beyond its own unit, but that unit's numbers, units, names, dates and negations are always re-checked.
Every declared source is pinned (revision where one exists, retrieval time, raw and text hashes); an unpinned source is an obligation; a changed snapshot is a defect.
An evidence span cited by a unit that does not resolve in its pinned snapshot is a defect; a retrieved reference without its pin is an obligation.
Source pinning runs in both profiles; instructor-supplied files are pinned by hash.
Rights, licence and attribution checks run only in public packages; private packages follow the Alembic contract and may be packed but are never cleared for public release.
There are exactly two use profiles, public and private.

Manifest, file layout, orz syntax (with nesting), each deliverable's framework notation (orz-slides deck grammar for slides, orz-paged settings for print documents — checked against the frameworks' own theme and template ids), placeholders and the accessibility floor are checked as defects; no word-presence test stands in for coverage.
Broken local links and asset paths are defects; external links are resolved, the result recorded, and replayed offline in tests.

Carriers are not a Coursewerk deliverable (D24): the package is lean orz Markdown; the harness documents how Alembic or an agent assembles carriers (docs/assembling-carriers.md), and the optional carrier preview can only raise questions.
A quotation found in no pinned or supplied source is an obligation; a misquotation is a defect; near-verbatim copying is a defect in public packages only.
The 21 v0.12.0 false positives on the C2 fixture (18 quoted spine misconceptions, 3 Mermaid labels) raise nothing.
The same term and dimension carrying different values after conversion and tolerance, an answer key disagreeing with its question, and a physically impossible quantity are defects.
A reworded definition raises nothing; definition-drift is retired.

The new gate has no misconception-asserted, revision-escalate or spine-relabeled check and does not require the whole-package key-fact review or the mandatory visual attestation; misconception detection, if it returns, returns only as a trial module.
Verifier tasks are dispatched per unit with a blind bundle (the unit and its evidence only); every dispatch is recorded and replays offline.
Retrieval sends only the claim being checked, pins what it retrieves (URL, time, hash, span), and can be switched off per package.
A semi-mechanical obligation is cleared only when the verifier's quote is found in the source and carries the same value, date or name.
A verifier response that cannot be parsed is recorded as unscorable, never as a pass or a miss.
The agent corrects without asking only a defect admitted by a stable check and uncontested; instructor text additionally needs two agreeing sources; otherwise a question is raised.
Every correction is logged as a revision and shown as a revertible diff at the next checkpoint (or at once when the instructor asked for the check).
requirements.reason: T1 closed (tests/verdict-path.test.mjs). No harness auto-correction occurred in the P10 live runs: the agent fixes its own drafts first (D31), and a correction needs an anchored, uncontested contradiction (two sources for instructor text). The live case is the study planted-fault runs (P11, K4); see system/rounds/P10-dogfood.md.

requirements.statement: An instructor reverting an agent's correction after seeing the diff and evidence is the double confirmation: a note is recorded and the text stands as an authorized divergence.
An unevidenced fact the instructor wrote is cleared by one confirmation, which can be batched.

Knowledge-based issues in the instructor's text or the approved spine are raised as questions with reasoning and a suggested revision, and change nothing until the instructor confirms; the agent may revise its own draft text in the work loop (D17, D31).
Each chapter is in exactly one state (DRAFT, ASSEMBLING, PACKAGE; PUBLISHED as a snapshot) and moves only by the listed triggers and preconditions.
A draft can be used as-is privately and is never published publicly.
The agent contacts the instructor only at the six moments M1–M6 (plus instructor-initiated exchanges).
The digest clusters questions by root cause, ranks them, caps them per batch, defers overflow (never drops it) and shows deferred counts; the list of corrections sits outside the budget.
An answered question is never asked again while its basis is unchanged.
The work loop stops at a fixed point or when the batch budget is spent, and never changes the spine, answers a question for the instructor, or reopens a recorded decision.
A publish decision is recorded with the snapshot hash, the approvals it relied on and the open questions listed.
Only chapters in PACKAGE with a valid approval are published, and the course map only with its own valid approval.
Public and private packages go through one gate; the profile toggles only the rights modules.
The documented commands (assemble, approve, status, digest, publish, revert) each refuse with a plain next step when their preconditions fail.
check_oer.mjs is no longer the gate; its remaining checks run as modules.
PROCEDURE, CLAUDE/AGENTS and the format contracts describe the skeleton as lean orientation; a context-blind agent can run the workflow from them alone.
Existing packages migrate by tool; the migrated spine is presented as a revision for approval, never converted silently.
The C2 chemistry package is migrated and taken end to end to a publish decision, with a report against the v0.12.0 baseline in which every false positive is fixed or explained.
An invisible format character (zero-width, bidi control, soft hyphen) in a deliverable is a defect: it hides values from every check that reads the text.

A general absolute ("only" with no comparison set named in words) is never cleared by quote evidence; a scoped one is admitted only when the member is affirmed and every named alternative is denied by a quote.

Every absolute statement (only, always, never, every, all, none) outside quoted misconceptions and scoped exclusivities is read by a logged context review before the gate passes; casual usage and context-scoped claims pass, an over-general scientific absolute is a question routed to the agent with a rewording — the instructor is not asked unless the agent cannot resolve it.
How every issue was found and how it was settled is rebuilt from the package's own records (verification records, corrections, unit index, decision log), with repeats folded and counted.

Open questions never block publishing (D14), but they are raised before it: with any open, publish lists them and stops; the instructor may publish over them in their own words, and the decision records that it was made over them.

The blind conceptual review reads each knowledge-based unit in place (up to two units before it and one after, as context only) and raises concerns only about the unit's own words; a concern's quote is matched with math and emphasis markup set aside.
requirements.source: D26; P11 dev cases (V10, NM04, DIR07)

requirements.statement: A deliverable's restated learning objectives must say what an approved objective of its chapter says (compared on prose words, so notation is not a difference); a difference is a defect routed to the agent.

The blind reviewer sorts concerns into 'wrong' and 'clarify' (correct as meant; a few words remove a likely misreading), judged at the course's level and within the passage's scope. A clarification of the agent's own text is the agent's to apply, with no question; of the instructor's text, a one-line diff the instructor accepts or not, after which applying it is owed by the agent and the instructor keeps the credit. Round 4 (R4-K16): whose text it is is decided before whether a suggestion is in it — on the instructor's text a suggestion (clarify or wrong) the agent wrote in without the instructor's 'apply' settles nothing: the concern's question stays theirs, and the edit itself is raised as instructor-edit-unasked (question, digest) until they accept the suggestion or answer it.

Carriers are assembled with the newest orz frames (orz-mdhtml, orz-slides, orz-paged, orz-markdown), installed into a frame cache outside the package and the harness; the versions used are recorded in the build receipt, never in the course. Unreachable registry: the installed frames, said so.

The user's preferences (~/.coursewerk) shape the materials (structure, depth, graphics tools, themes) and never the 3C checks: no check reads them, and the gate's findings are identical with any preferences.

Before a v2 package is packed, Alembic's own validator, fetched at the package contract's newest commit from the Alembic repository, must accept it; the commit is reported with the pack. Offline, the pack says it was checked only against the local mirror.

An instructor's answer to a disputed fact is bound to the claim itself (unit, claim sentence, disputed values), not the whole unit: an edit elsewhere in the unit never re-asks it, and a kept claim counts as settled for that claim while every other claim still needs its own evidence.

At re-approval, the spine lines changed since the last approval (concept map and assessment guide: req.spine.blind-review-diff) are reviewed by a context-blind verifier (accuracy only, wrong/clarify); its concerns are questions in the approval preview and never edit the spine; re-approval waits for the review unless the agent records that it was approved without it (offline).

Links are verified, not trusted (C2, C3): a context-blind reviewer reads each linked teaching unit with its declared spine links and the chapter's plan; a link it does not teach is a question for the agent (link-doubtful), a unit that teaches nothing in the plan is a question for the instructor (off-spine). Trial module: questions only, never blocking. Records bind to the unit's text, its links and the linked nodes' text.

Assessment follows the guide in kind and level (C5 fidelity): the same review judges whether a practice question is the type and cognitive level its guide entry prescribes; a mismatch is a question (assessment-fidelity) for the agent in agent text, for the instructor in theirs. Trial, never blocking.

C1 — Every approved objective is taught: closed loop on the real course (plant the violation → the expected finding, routed to the right party → the routed fix → the finding set returns to the baseline).

C2 — Links are verified, not trusted: closed loop on the real course (plant the violation → the expected finding, routed to the right party → the routed fix → the finding set returns to the baseline).

C3 — Nothing off-spine goes unnoticed: closed loop on the real course (plant the violation → the expected finding, routed to the right party → the routed fix → the finding set returns to the baseline).
C4 — The spine is a restoring force: closed loop on the real course (plant the violation → the expected finding, routed to the right party → the routed fix → the finding set returns to the baseline).
C5 — Assessment follows the guide: closed loop on the real course (plant the violation → the expected finding, routed to the right party → the routed fix → the finding set returns to the baseline).
K1 — Level 1 is complete: closed loop on the real course (plant the violation → the expected finding, routed to the right party → the routed fix → the finding set returns to the baseline).
K2 — Computable content is checked: closed loop on the real course (plant the violation → the expected finding, routed to the right party → the routed fix → the finding set returns to the baseline).
K3 — Every reported defect is real: closed loop on the real course (plant the violation → the expected finding, routed to the right party → the routed fix → the finding set returns to the baseline).
K4 — No harmful revision: closed loop on the real course (plant the violation → the expected finding, routed to the right party → the routed fix → the finding set returns to the baseline).

K5 — Convergence: concerns never block; revised they are history: closed loop on the real course (plant the violation → the expected finding, routed to the right party → the routed fix → the finding set returns to the baseline).

K6 — Level 2 best effort: concerns on the instructor's text are theirs, never edits: closed loop on the real course (plant the violation → the expected finding, routed to the right party → the routed fix → the finding set returns to the baseline).

H1 — The impact of a change is found: closed loop on the real course (plant the violation → the expected finding, routed to the right party → the routed fix → the finding set returns to the baseline).
H2 — Nothing is silently stranded: closed loop on the real course (plant the violation → the expected finding, routed to the right party → the routed fix → the finding set returns to the baseline).

H3 — A change that changes nothing raises nothing: closed loop on the real course (plant the violation → the expected finding, routed to the right party → the routed fix → the finding set returns to the baseline).
H4 — Identity survives revision: closed loop on the real course (plant the violation → the expected finding, routed to the right party → the routed fix → the finding set returns to the baseline).
H5 — The record holds: closed loop on the real course (plant the violation → the expected finding, routed to the right party → the routed fix → the finding set returns to the baseline).

One value parser (F1–F4, F7, F10): the claim extractor and the semi-mechanical classifier read values through core/values.mjs over the harness's unit table (lib/units.mjs) — mmHg, kcal, °F, V …; thousands separators; every typeset minus; scientific notation with its mantissa, exactly; units with their denominators (kJ/mol ≠ kJ/g ≠ kJ); dimensionless values bound to a symbol (K, K_p, pH) and powers of ten are required tokens. A correction never doubles a sign. Round 2 (R2-K04, K05, K07): the unit table's ordinary spelled and plural forms (kilojoules, kilocalories, calories, atmospheres, metres, litres …) and psi, eV, hPa and the tonne are units; HTML character references (−, −, −, – …) are decoded before values are read. Round 3 (R3-K01, K07): bars, kbar, mbar, GPa, ksi and Torr are units; a symbol's subscript in any LaTeX spelling (K_{p}, K_\mathrm{p}, K<sub>p</sub>) is the symbol; a sign written as a word (minus, negative, plus, positive) or outside a bracket (−(63.7), (−63.7)) is a sign; an HTML <sup> exponent is an exponent with any minus. Round 4 (R4-K13/K14): a sign carried by a verb is read — an energy a verb in the same clause says is released (given off, evolved, liberated, emitted, produced) reads negative and one absorbed (taken in, taken up) positive, as the enthalpy change it states: written number × the verb's sign ('92.2 kJ of heat is released' = −92.2 kJ, literally '−92.2 kJ … released' = +92.2 kJ); a value bound to a symbol ('ΔH = −92.2 kJ, so heat is released') keeps its written sign.
requirements.source: 3C red team round 1, CONFIDENCE (operator design direction, 2026-10-06)

requirements.statement: Support checks the predicate, not only the tokens (F5, F6, F8): a quote stating the opposite direction (left/right, toward reactants/products, increase/decrease, endothermic/exothermic) never supports; a sentence-initial lone surname as the subject of an attribution is a required name; an equation claim's reaction is required — the quote must state the same reaction. Round 2 (R2-K01–K03): magnitude words (large/small, high/low, mostly/little, fast/slow, strong/weak, positive/negative …) are directions too, read over the whole quote and beside the content word they modify; a claim that negates a predicate its quote asserts, or asserts one its quote negates, is not supported; a quantity the claim names in words (free energy, enthalpy, entropy, equilibrium constant, rate constant …) must be the quantity the quote names. A doubt is a refusal (evidence stays missing), never an admission.
requirements.source: 3C red team round 1, CONFIDENCE (operator design direction, 2026-10-06)

requirements.statement: Reaction anchoring compares stoichiometry (coefficients, fractions included; a scaled equation is another equation) and the quantity named (ΔH vs ΔG° vs K): a mismatch never anchors a contradiction, so a correct value is never a defect nor auto-corrected (F9, F10). Round 2 (R2-K06): an equation is read in \mathrm{}/\text{} math and in plain Unicode or ASCII (⇌ → <=> ->), not only in \ce{}; a claim that writes its reaction is anchored only by a quote stating the same reaction — a lead-in's name never anchors a contradiction onto it.
requirements.source: 3C red team round 1, CONFIDENCE (operator design direction, 2026-10-06)

requirements.statement: A scanned sentence naming several key terms still compares each value under the term that governs it (the nearest mention before it in its sentence), so a second key term cannot hide a value disagreement (F11).
requirements.source: 3C red team round 1, CONFIDENCE (operator design direction, 2026-10-06)

requirements.statement: A concern is settled by the text only when the unit carries the suggestion and no longer carries the concern's quoted words, unless the suggestion extends them: a deletion-type fix is never 'already applied' while the wrong words stand (F12). Round 3 (R3-K06): a 'wrong' concern whose words are gone is settled only when a fresh review of the unit's current text (contentHash) was logged after it — a review that clears it — or its suggestion went in place of its words and the unit's text changed nowhere else. A synonym swap or any other rewording that removes the words keeps it open; the newest review of a unit always speaks for it, so a rewrite that changes a fact token cannot silence it. Round 4 (R4-K15): the newest review of the unit's current text (contentHash) speaks for the unit: every older review is history, whether or not its quoted words remain — an error fixed at its cause with the quoted words kept is cleared by a clean fresh review.
requirements.source: 3C red team round 1, CONFIDENCE (operator design direction, 2026-10-06)

requirements.statement: Open concerns travel with the text (red-team round 4, R4-K17): the unit index records on every unit the units whose text it took over (lineage: the pieces of a split, a merge, a piece of a retired unit), kept for good and in the retired-unit register as what a unit owed is; a knowledge review of a retired unit speaks for each unit of its lineage, for the quoted words that unit holds, until a fresh review of that unit's current text is logged after it.

Quote evidence for an equation binds the lead-in it was verified with: a changed lead-in makes the evidence stale (evidence-missing, the agent's), never a stranded defect, and the routed fix (verify semi) re-dispatches and clears it (F13).
requirements.source: 3C red team round 1, CONFIDENCE (operator design direction, 2026-10-06)

requirements.statement: The verifier's 'hypothetical' label is trusted only for exercise-like units (questions, answers, worked-example or practice sections); elsewhere it is no evidence and no question — the evidence stays missing and nothing recommends 'confirm' (F14). Round 2 (R2-K09): exercise-likeness comes from the unit's form and role (a question or answer, a practice deliverable, a worked-example or exercise section), never from a cue word in its text.
requirements.source: 3C red team round 1, CONFIDENCE (operator design direction, 2026-10-06)

requirements.statement: An instructor's digest answer asking for a change to a disputed fact (anything but keep/confirm/later) is routed to the agent as a blocking obligation (instructor-change-owed) until the claim's sentence changes; the old evidence no longer counts for that claim (F15).
requirements.source: 3C red team round 1, CONFIDENCE (operator design direction, 2026-10-06)

requirements.statement: An auto-correction replaces a value's sign or prefix together with its number (+, −, a spaced minus, − …), and the corrected text must read as the source's value with one sign: a correction that would produce a malformed value ('+−92.2', '−−92.2', '0 - −92.2') is refused and becomes the instructor's question (round 2, K06/K07). Round 3 (R3-K02): a sign word is replaced with the number ('minus 63.7 kJ' → '−92.2 kJ'); the corrected text is re-read with the full parser, and a sign word beside a signed number is malformed and refused. Round 4 (R4-K13): beside a sign verb a correction writes the magnitude only ('63.7 kJ of heat is released' → '92.2 kJ of heat is released'), a sign written there goes with the old number, a source of the sign opposite to the verb's is a question, and a corrected text with a signed number beside a sign verb is refused as malformed.
requirements.source: 3C red team round 2, CONFIDENCE (operator design direction, 2026-10-06)

requirements.statement: MS7 (value consistency and the range audit) reads values through the one value parser, core/values.mjs, never its own regex: every minus form (spaced, typeset, HTML), thousands separators, and denominators (kJ mol^{-1} is kJ/mol) — so a sign disagreement or a molar-energy disagreement is a value-disagreement (round 2, R2-K08).
requirements.source: 3C red team round 2, CONFIDENCE (operator design direction, 2026-10-06)

requirements.statement: A knowledge concern's quote is located in the passage as written or as a reader sees it (rendered math: ΔH < 0 for $\Delta H < 0$). A concern whose words the reviewed passage does not contain, or an answer that cannot be read, makes the review unscorable (knowledge-unscorable, the agent's): it is never counted as a clean review — not for review coverage, not to clear an owed re-verification (round 2, R2-K10).
requirements.source: 3C red team round 2, CONFIDENCE (operator design direction, 2026-10-06)

requirements.statement: An absolute-statement review counts only through what the decision log binds: the unit, sentences, context and nonce are read from the logged prompt (bundleHash) and the answer from the logged response (responseHash) — never from the record's editable fields — and a record whose log entry carries a recordHash must match it (round 2, Control attacker's handoff: 29 pre-round-1 records had no recordHash).
requirements.source: 3C red team round 2, CONFIDENCE (operator design direction, 2026-10-06)

requirements.statement: A unitless shared value is bound through the one value parser as well as 'symbol = value': 'whose K is 50', 'K of 50', 'K equals 50', 'K ≈ 50' bind K to 50, so a changed K reaches every unit stating it (round 2, Coherence F7).
requirements.source: 3C red team round 2, CONFIDENCE (operator design direction, 2026-10-06)

requirements.statement: MS9 reads, for each unit, the latest (in log order) of its logged link reviews whose basis matches the unit as it is now; an older current review is not hidden by a newer one made stale by an edit and its revert.

A dispatch's whole record is bound into its log entry (recordHash): an edit of any field — an alignment record's declared items, its alignmentBasis, its time — makes it a dispatch the log does not vouch for (dispatch-unlogged, a blocking defect). MS9 re-derives what a review declared from the unit, never from the record.

The link review fails closed: verdicts and fidelity words are read case-insensitively; a declared link the answer omits, a word that is no verdict, a fidelity the harness cannot read, an off-plan answer that is not an explicit true or false, or an unscorable answer is a question (alignment-unscorable, route agent); a framing unit whose review leaves the off-plan answer unanswered still owes its review; an unreadable re-run does not hide an earlier readable verdict.
requirements.source: 3C red team round 1, CONTROL (studies/p11/redteam/control, 2026-10-06) C2-16; 3C red team round 2, CONTROL (studies/p11/redteam-r2/control, 2026-10-06) C2-13

requirements.statement: Review and coverage read the same set: answers count toward objective coverage (a study guide's worked-example Solution teaches), so the link review reads every linked teaching unit, answers included, each with its question as context.

An approved course-map objective is covered only by what is taught (D41): a chapter objective or concept that names it in [prereq: …] AND that a unit's current blind link review says it teaches, or a study-guide/slides unit linking the course objective itself, reviewed "yes". A [prereq: …] mention alone covers nothing (round 2 C1-10); an unreviewed candidate is link-review-owed; otherwise course-objective-uncovered.
requirements.source: 3C red team round 1, CONTROL (studies/p11/redteam/control, 2026-10-06) C1-10; 3C red team round 2, CONTROL (studies/p11/redteam-r2/control, 2026-10-06) C1-10

requirements.statement: A guide entry is for questions: a teaching unit that is neither a question nor an answer and links only guide entries is unit-unlinked; it is still reviewed, its declared items being the entries and the entries' objectives.

Only the list items of a Learning objectives section (any heading level; the section runs to the next heading of its level or higher, `#` counted as `##`, a slide marker or a rule) are structure; other prose in it is segmented into units, and every list item in it is read by the restated-objective check.
A unit's role is re-derived from its text and structure (the segmenter; framing may not carry facts) by loadUnits and MS9; a role in the sidecar is never trusted.

Restated objectives are compared with the approved ones on their full text, maths included, with notation normalized (LaTeX and Unicode, spacing, emphasis, punctuation) but case kept (ln K is not ln k); trailing [anchor: …]/[prereq: …] groups must be the node's own, and any other bracketed text is part of the text; every approved objective must be restated where the section exists (objective-not-restated); a `#` Learning objectives heading is read like `##`.
requirements.source: 3C red team round 1, CONTROL (studies/p11/redteam/control, 2026-10-06) C4-12; 3C red team round 2, CONTROL (studies/p11/redteam-r2/control, 2026-10-06) C4-09

requirements.statement: A spine change that changes a direction word (fewer/more, raise/lower …: meaningTokens, in order) is substantive, never light; `coursewerk.mjs approve` and `spine.mjs approve` share one precondition (approvalPrecondition: a well-formed spine and the blind review of the changed lines, D39, or a recorded --without-review).

Each practice question counts toward one guide entry's Count: guide-entry-short is computed on a maximum matching of questions to the entries' Count slots, so a question linked to several entries fills only one.
The level review checks a practice question against every guide entry it is linked to (one fidelity answer per entry, by id); an entry left unanswered is a question (alignment-unscorable).
Only questions in practice/ count toward a guide entry's Count; a study guide's worked example (its solution printed beside it) does not.

spine check (and so approval and the gate) refuses guide text the grammar does not read: an anchored heading that is not a ### entry under a ## … [objective: …] section, and entry fields under no entry (an untagged section, a #### sub-entry); a sub-entry never overwrites its parent's fields.

A stamp is not a re-verification: an owed re-verification or version carry survives edits, relinks and re-indexing (also through a split or merge, and a retire-and-return), and clears only through a logged blind correctness re-check of the unit's current text and dependencies made after it arose (units.mjs reverify, which refuses otherwise and names the review to run; a review that found the text wrong does not count; a link review never counts), or the instructor's confirmation.
requirements.source: red team R1 coherence (2026-10-06): F4, F5, F14; R2 F6, F9

requirements.statement: A re-check owed because a dependency moved is shown what moved: the knowledge-review bundle of such a unit carries each moved target as it is now (the unit stating a shared value, a key term's definition, a spine node's text, a question it answers or names), and units.mjs reverify counts only a review whose logged prompt carried every one of them.

No exported writer clears an obligation on the caller's word: every unit-record write (writeUnitRecords) is compared with the records on disk, and a write that clears what a unit owes (a moved target, an owes entry, a version carry, or the record itself) is refused unless the unit is stamped as it stands now and the evidence is logged — a counted blind re-check (as reverify requires) or the instructor's confirmation since the record was last written. admitEvidence admits only evidence from a logged fact check of that unit at the facts it claims (or of a logged auto-correction of it).

An answer is bound to the question its label names ("Answer 6" to "Q 6"; by position only when there are no labels, and a label beats position) by the question's id and the hash of its wording as a reader sees it (the light key of the rendered text: struck, hidden and link-destination text dropped; case, whitespace, emphasis, list markers and prose punctuation folded; every sign, relation, arrow and operator kept): any rewording or re-pairing makes the answer owe a re-check, routed to the agent as a cheap blind re-review, never to the instructor's digest; a legacy stamp without the binding owes it once and is never baselined by upgradeStamps; the still-correct finding is bound to the question's wording; the knowledge and link reviews read an answer with the same question. A stamp written with the pre-R4 key migrates once: it counts as current only where the question's text is unchanged under both keys (the old-key hash matches and the text holds nothing the old key folded that the new key reads), and otherwise owes one re-check.
requirements.source: red team R1 coherence (2026-10-06): F1, F2, F3, F7, F15; R2 F13; R4 coherence F5

requirements.statement: Key-term dependencies are matched on the text as written AND as a reader sees it (rendered: emphasis, links and markup gone, so "**Endothermic** reaction" is a use), and are one target per map that defines the term (term:<chapter or course>:<label>; a label defined in two maps is two targets), and match the label's plural (s/es), either apostrophe and declared aliases ([alias: …] or the glossary parenthetical), also in their LaTeX spellings ($Q_r$, Q_{r}, \mathrm{Q_r}), a short alias in its own case; a unitless symbol=value binding (K = 50, Q_r = 50, pH = 7) is a shared value between the units stating it, its symbol read as its family (K, K_{eq}, K_c, K_\mathrm{eq}, Keq are one symbol; a symbol not starting with a capital is kept whole); a question or answer named by number is a dependency bound to its full wording, of the unit naming it and of that unit's answer, resolved as the knowledge review resolves it — in every spelling: Q3, Q 3, Q.3, Question #3, Problem #3, Prob. 3, Ex. 3, item 3, question three (number words to twenty), and every number of a list or range (Questions 3 and 4, questions 3–5, Q3–Q5). A reference WITHOUT a number ("the same reaction", "the previous question", "the reaction above", "the reaction in Q…", "this reaction") is a dependency on the nearest question before it in its deliverable and on the nearest unit before it that writes a reaction (fail toward an edge). Stamps written before R4 migrate once with no work when nothing changed: a label-only term key stands for every map's definition, each baselined at its map's last full approval before the unit's record was last written; a term edge the stamp never held is baselined the same way.
requirements.source: red team R1 coherence (2026-10-06): F8, F11; R2 F3, F12; R3 coherence F3, F5; R4 coherence F1, F2, F6

requirements.statement: Every harness write of a unit record logs a digest of the whole sidecar it wrote (locator, register and every other field); a sidecar that differs from its last logged digest is a blocking defect, the harness refuses to write over it (no laundering by re-index), and logUnitRecords refuses to log over it; the gate recomputes a unit's deliverable, section and place from the text.
requirements.source: red team R1 coherence (2026-10-06): F6; R2 F8, F10

requirements.statement: The pack ships only what the publish content hash binds, plus the log; the decision record it ships is rebuilt from the logged decision, and an on-disk record that differs from the log is refused.

Every committed version of the decision log extends the version committed in each of its parents, for every commit reachable from HEAD (an orphan merged in with -s ours is caught); the log at every anchor (HEAD's reflog, every local branch and its reflog, remote-tracking branches, tags) is an earlier version of the current log (the current history extends it); a release receipt names the log's last record: a later pack refuses a log, or a HEAD whose committed log, that no longer holds it, and the gate reads the receipt beside the package (dist/) as an anchor. A rewrite onto a new root with every anchor removed is out of reach (documented in gate.mjs). Every git call of the log and history checks runs with object replacement off (--no-replace-objects, GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1) and no graft file, and a package whose git has refs/replace/* or info/grafts is log-broken.
requirements.source: red team R1 coherence (2026-10-06): F10; R2 F5; R3 coherence F7; R4 coherence F3

requirements.statement: A new major version is not opened while any deliverable in its scope has edits not yet indexed, so every unit of the scope is carried.

A spine or key-term change is light only when old and new differ ONLY by whitespace, `*`/`_` emphasis, list markers, letter case and prose punctuation that is not a sign, relation, arrow or operator, compared on the RENDERED text (orz-markdown): struck-through (~~…~~, <del>, <s>, <strike>), commented-out and hidden words and a link's destination are not there. Every other character change is at least a rephrasing; a change among the signs, relations, arrows and operators a reader sees (−, -, –, －, ⁻, ⁺, ±, ↑/↓, ≪/≫, ⩽/⩾, < > = ≤ ≥, `/` and `*`, `^` and `_`, sub- and superscripts, \ce{->}/\ce{<-}, ⇌ → ← ⇒) is substantive. A change of words that keeps every value, name, number, sign, negation and direction word is a rephrasing: a glance confirms it only when the current D39 blind review says every changed line says the same as the approved text it replaces and that the plan still says every removed approved line; a line judged changed, an unanswered meaning, nothing to ask about, or no review means full re-approval (D43). A light change whose current review says a line changed is not glanced, and no glance is given while the current review raises a "wrong" concern. Any other change is substantive. A light or meaning-kept, glance-confirmed change raises no re-verification: spine node, guide entry and key-term targets keep counting at their hash from the last full approval; a substantive change still makes linked units owe re-verification.
requirements.source: red team R1 coherence (2026-10-06): F13; R2 F4; R3 coherence F1, F6; R3 control C4-01, C4-02; R4 coherence F8; R4 control C4-01

requirements.statement: An identity break forgets nothing: a retired unit's record (stamp, owed re-verification, version carry, links, origin, evidence) is kept in its deliverable's unit record; a text that comes back byte for byte or nearly (same form, token overlap ≥ 0.5) in ANY deliverable of the package (its own deliverable's retired units first) takes back its id and record, a piece of a retired unit or a text covering one, in any deliverable, inherits its stamp and obligations (as split and merge pieces do), and a retired id is never minted for other text.
requirements.source: red team R2 coherence (2026-10-06): F1, F2, F14; R3 coherence F4

requirements.statement: No exported call clears an obligation without evidence: re-verification counts only a correctness review (knowledge; an admitting semi for a non-answer) whose dispatch record is the one the log vouches for (record, prompt and answer hashes), is of the unit's current text, showed that text (and an answer's question) and holds a readable answer; there is no module-name clearing path; admitted evidence names a logged fact-check dispatch.
requirements.source: red team R2 coherence (2026-10-06): F6, F9, F10

requirements.statement: D41: an objective counts as taught only when a unit's current blind link review judges that it teaches it; an unreviewed covering link is the agent's review owed (link-review-owed, blocking); links only 'in passing' do not cover; offline, a publish may set the owed reviews aside and the decision records which.

D42: everything that ships is checked — framing units are read for off-plan content (framing-review-owed until read; off-plan → the instructor's question); documents declared in DOCUMENTS.json are deliverables unless the instructor confirmed them administrative (req.ship.administrative-instructor); an orz-paged settings or metadata block is notation.

Structure is only what the frame does not print: text after a comment's "-->", `###`–`######` headings, a `#`/`##` heading or table header that reads as sentences, a header-only table, a credit-line paragraph that carries more than a short single attribution line, and every {{nyml}} block but the orz-paged settings and metadata blocks (document, meta) are units, segmented, linked and reviewed like any other.
requirements.source: 3C red team round 2, CONTROL (studies/p11/redteam-r2/control, 2026-10-06) C3-01, C3-02, C3-03, C3-05

requirements.statement: Whether a line prints is orz-markdown's call, read from its own token stream (core/printed.mjs), not the segmenter's line grammar: a line the grammar took for structure that orz prints is a unit (prose inside a tab group outside every tab, text after a {{nyml}} block orz closed at the first line holding "}}"), unless it is a bounded printed label: a `#`/`##` label heading only while it heads content before the next heading of its level or slide marker (a section-template slide heads the slides up to the next framing-template slide); a `::: spoil`/`::: tab` label only as a label over a non-empty body; one credit line per deliverable (two or more are each a unit).
requirements.source: 3C red team round 3, CONTROL (studies/p11/redteam-r3/control, 2026-10-07) C3-03, C3-04, C3-06

requirements.statement: Text hidden from the student never counts: in a deliverable, raw HTML outside the visible phrasing set (any hidden/style/class attribute, <details>, <template>, <style>, <noscript> …), a comment inside printed text, a `<!…>`/`<?…>` declaration, maths that typesets invisibly (\phantom, \color), or a unit orz-markdown prints nothing of is content-hidden, a blocking defect for the agent, and the pack refuses it.

What ships and what is checked are one computation (shipped.mjs): every markdown file the pack would ship is a deliverable, the spine, an instructor-confirmed administrative document or a harness record — otherwise document-unchecked (a blocking defect) and the pack refuses; a {{md}}/{{markdown}}/{{md-include}} include must name a deliverable (read on its own), otherwise include-unchecked and the pack refuses; an include is every form orz-markdown renders (read from its token stream: one line, [args], the path on its own lines up to "}}", inside containers, lists and quotes).
requirements.source: 3C red team round 2, CONTROL (studies/p11/redteam-r2/control, 2026-10-06) C3-04, C3-07; 3C red team round 3, CONTROL (studies/p11/redteam-r3/control, 2026-10-07) C3-07

requirements.statement: `role: administrative` in DOCUMENTS.json exempts a document from the deliverable checks only while a logged instructor confirmation (coursewerk.mjs administrative, quoting their words) names it at its current content; the field alone, or an edit after the confirmation, leaves it a deliverable.

D41 for the assessment guide: a practice question fills an entry's Count only when its current blind review says it practises the entry's objective ("yes") and has answered the entry's type and level — a type or level that differs is the instructor's assessment-fidelity question and never leaves a Count short (D44); a framing question never fills one; a Count short only of reviews owed is link-review-owed (the agent's), otherwise guide-entry-short.

The D39 review that lets a re-approval through is the logged spine-review dispatch — its record vouched for by the log (recordHash), made of the current text and exactly the current changed lines; its concerns are re-read from the answer. A file under metadata/spine/review/ is a copy and satisfies nothing. Its meaning answer is bound to its baseline: the full approval it diffed against (seq and hash) and exactly the lines it was asked about, changed and removed — a review answered against one approved text is never current against another.
requirements.source: 3C red team round 2, CONTROL (studies/p11/redteam-r2/control, 2026-10-06) C4-11; R3 coherence F2

requirements.statement: The D39 changed lines are a longest-common-subsequence diff of every file the approval covers (a chapter's concept map and assessment guide; the course map), each line keyed by its text and the headings it stands under: a reworded, added or moved line, or a line under a renamed heading, is changed; renumbering a list is not.

A link or framing review is bound to the plan items it judged (a linked unit: its links, declared items and guide entries; framing: the whole plan it was shown) and to their text as the instructor last fully approved it while the current approval is a glance-confirmed light change: an edit of another plan item, or a confirmed light rewording, voids no review; a real change to a judged item voids it. Records made before round 2 stay current under their whole-plan basis.

The D43 meaning question covers every approved line a change removed as well as every line it added or changed: the blind review is shown each removed line, marked "(removed)", and asked whether the plan still says it; a change made only of deletions is never "the same" by default, and a change with nothing to ask about is never glanceable as a rephrasing.
requirements.source: 3C red team round 3, COHERENCE F1 and CONTROL C4-01 (studies/p11/redteam-r3, 2026-10-07)

requirements.statement: A "wrong" concern the current D39 spine review raises about a changed plan line reaches the gate as the instructor's question (skeleton spine-review-concern, routed to the digest, never blocking), for as long as that review is current — not only in the approval preview a glance skips.
requirements.source: 3C red team round 3, CONTROL C4-02 and COHERENCE F6 (studies/p11/redteam-r3, 2026-10-07)

requirements.statement: A unit that names a question or answer by number is bound to the units its reference resolved to when it was stamped: when a stamped reference is no longer an edge (a renumbering made the number name another unit, or none), the unit owes a re-check (reference-binding:re-targeted). References only added beside every stamped one (a spelling the harness newly reads) are baselined.

The value parser fails closed (R3-K01): a number followed by a unit-like token the unit table does not hold (mixed case like GPa or kDa, a short lowercase token like ppm, a short capitalised one like Torr — never an English word, a count, a label or a chemical formula) is a value with an OPAQUE unit, kept as written: the sentence is semi-mechanical and owes evidence, and a quote must carry the same number and token. An opaque unit is never converted or compared across units. A value the parser reads in a semi sentence that an honest quote contradicts is a contradiction (fact-contradicted), not evidence-missing. Round 4 (R4-K08): a number written in words straight before a unit of the table ('two thousand atmospheres', 'nine hundred kilojoules per mole', 'twenty-five degrees Celsius') is read as its digits, so the sentence is semi-mechanical and owes evidence; a small count of moles in words ('four moles of gas') stays a coefficient.

The semi-mechanical classifier's name trigger is the claim extractor's own name reader (core/names.mjs namesIn), less a name used only as an eponymous term ('the Gibbs energy', 'the van 't Hoff equation', 'the Haber process'), which asserts nothing about the person: 'the work of Arrhenius' is a fact that owes evidence (R3-K01). A list marker or a value's unit is never a name.

K2: computable content is checked (R3-K03, R4-K01/K02/K03/K07/K11/K12). At V4/V6/V8 the gate reads every worked chain in math ($…$, $$…$$, \(…\), \[…\], and aligned/align/gather/split environments, whose '&' and '\\' are layout; a span or line that opens with a relation continues the chain) and compares EVERY link between two numeric parts: arithmetic with a literal at the literal's written precision, arithmetic with arithmetic (a restatement, held to what its rounded inputs allow), and a literal with a literal; both beyond half a percent before a disagreement counts. It reads numbers, scientific notation, + − × · / \frac ^ \sqrt \ln \log \exp, brackets, implicit products, =, ≈, \approx, \sim, and '\%' as the percent unit (a percent on one side only holds under either reading). Units are compared by meaning through the shared unit table ('mol/L', 'mol L^{-1}' and 'M' are one unit); a real change of unit is not converted. What cannot be read without a guess — a unit inside the arithmetic, e^x, an n-th root, an implicit product after '/' — is skipped AND counted (runGate's `mechanical`, the gate's notChecked), never passed in silence. A mismatch is a defect routed to the agent (computation-mismatch) with the recomputed value in its evidence. A unit the instructor confirmed is not re-raised only at the text confirmed (contentHash): any edit voids the exemption. The real course (C2) raises none.
requirements.source: 3C red team rounds 3 and 4, CONFIDENCE (studies/p11/redteam-r3/confidence, redteam-r4/confidence)

requirements.statement: K2: every reaction a unit writes is balanced by a dedicated reaction reader (R3-K03, R4-K04/K05/K06/K09/K10), not the claim reader that identifies a reaction: each \ce{…} with an arrow (braces matched; mhchem arrow conditions such as '->[MnO2]' or '<=>[a][b]' dropped, never read as a species; states, hydrates, '+ heat'), and every reaction written outside \ce{} (\mathrm/\text math, prose, Unicode sub- and superscripts), not only the first. Ion charges are kept in every notation ('Ag+', 'Cu^2+', '^{3+}', '^{-}', 'Fe³⁺'); bracketed complexes and electrons are read; a caret-less 'NH4+' or 'Fe3+' is read both ways and is unbalanced only when no reading balances. A nuclear equation is balanced in mass and atomic number. An unbalanced element, charge, mass or atomic number is a defect routed to the agent (equation-unbalanced). A species that does not parse, a nuclide without its atomic number, or a side that continues past what is read skips the equation and is counted as not checked — never reported unbalanced. Correct ionic equilibria raise none; the real course (C2) raises none.

D30 absolutes are not a closed word list (R3-K04): only, solely, exclusively, alone, always, never, every, each, any, all, none, nothing, nobody, no one, invariably, universally, necessarily, inevitably, unconditionally, without exception, in all/every/any cases, under all conditions, regardless of, no matter, whatever, whenever, wherever, everything, everyone, everywhere owe a context review. Text in double quotes is exempt only as a quoted misconception: introduced as what someone says, thinks or claims, or followed at once by a correction (No…, Not…, but…, In fact…, it depends…, Evaluate this claim…); a scare-quoted word in the author's own claim counts.

Every verification record is read through what the decision log binds (R3-K05, K08): a record logged with its recordHash is bound whole; a record logged before round 1 (no recordHash) binds only its dispatch, unit, kind, prompt, answer and logged status, so its currency is DERIVED — a knowledge review's contentHash and factHash from the passage its prompt showed, a semi record's from the claims its prompt printed, an absolute review's from its printed sentences — and its admission is the logged status. Nothing counts through a field that cannot be derived. This holds in MS8, unreviewedKnowledge, liveContradictions (a confirmation is refused over a live contradiction) and the correction guard.

Whether text shows is the FRAME's call (orz-mdhtml, orz-slides, orz-paged with their stylesheets), not orz-markdown's alone (core/printed.mjs): a `::: tab` outside a `:::: tabs` group, a container class off the allowlist (success, info, warning, danger, left, right, center, spoil, tabs, tab, cols, col), a plugin block off the allowlist of kinds known to print (yaml/yml, test-block, {{nyml}} elements outside orz-paged, any unknown kind), an inline plugin that drops its text ({{attrs …text}}, {{space text}}, test-inline) or sets a class that may hide ({{sp[class]}} off the colour/badge set), a {{attrs[…]}} setting anything but an id or the step-reveal class, and a unit line that prints nothing (a link reference definition) are content-hidden, a blocking defect for the agent; speaker notes (`<!-- @notes -->` to the next region or slide) print nothing on a slide and are no unit, so they never count toward coverage; text before the first slide marker prints nothing; the deck config values orz-slides prints are read — `footer:` and `author:` as framing units, `title:` as a unit unless it is a label.
requirements.source: 3C red team round 4, CONTROL (studies/p11/redteam-r4/control and control-c245, 2026-10-07) C1-01, C1-02, C3-01 and the items seen but not developed

requirements.statement: A spine list item (objective, concept, misconception, key term, course-map item, guide field) is its marker line AND every continuation line orz-markdown reads as part of the same item (indented, lazy or a further paragraph); its bracket groups are read wherever its lines break. The whole item is the node's text, so it is the review basis and the review prompt's plan, and the restated-objective check compares the whole item (a deliverable's restated objectives read lazy continuation lines too). A nested item stays its own item; a one-line item reads exactly as before.
requirements.source: 3C red team round 4, CONTROL (studies/p11/redteam-r4/control and control-c245, 2026-10-07) C2-01

requirements.statement: Guide Counts are ONE maximum matching of practice questions over every chapter's guide entries, so a question linked to entries of two chapters fills one Count, never one in each; and whether the Counts are met is judged on the whole matching: when the verified matching is smaller than the total Count need, every question the possible (verified or owed) matching relies on that owes its review is link-review-owed, whatever the order of its links; an entry the possible matching cannot fill is guide-entry-short.
requirements.source: 3C red team round 4, CONTROL (studies/p11/redteam-r4/control and control-c245, 2026-10-07) C5-01, C5-02

requirements.statement: Every binding about what a reader reads is derived from ONE reader view (scripts/lib/core/rendered.mjs): the text as orz-markdown renders it (struck, hidden, commented and link-destination/title text out; entities decoded; invisible characters out; NFC) with each formula as KaTeX typesets it (grouping braces, spacing and sizing commands and one-glyph synonyms vanish; every sign, relation, arrow, script, font and symbol kept). Link/framing review currency and absolute-review currency are bound to its meaning key; the answer-to-question and reference bindings and the D43 light test to its light key (letter case folded); a `unit:` dependency to the fact tokens a reader sees. If the reader sees a different word or symbol the binding changes; if the reader sees the same thing it does not. Records keyed on earlier normalisations are upgraded where the text is unchanged under both keys, otherwise one cheap re-check is owed. Identity and evidence keys (contentHash, factHash on evidence, knowledge-review passages, instructor confirmations) stay on the source by design (D17).
requirements.source: 3C red team round 5, cause 1 (D46): Control C2-01, Coherence F5, F7, the 'does [](not) shift' note

requirements.statement: What a deck shows is orz-slides' own parse and render, not a parallel grammar (core/printed.mjs slideRegionsShown): parseDeck splits each slide's regions and renderSlide, run with a recording markdown renderer, decides which reach the slide — a region named outside the layout (any name the frame accepts), a repeated region name (the frame keeps the last), anything but `body` on a template slide, and an overwritten `@footer` print nothing, and a unit read there is content-hidden with the frame's reason; a repeated `@notes` stays notes. A table row is compared with the cells markdown-it renders: text beyond the header's column count is dropped by the frame, so the row is content-hidden. The notation check reads region markers with the frame's own pattern (asserted equal to the installed orz-slides') and reports a repeated region name.
requirements.source: 3C red team round 5 (studies/p11/redteam-r5/control and coherence, 2026-10-08) C1-01, C1-02

requirements.statement: A label is exempt from being a unit only when the whole label set is label-sized: a table header ROW (all its cells together), not each cell. Every label that prints and is no unit — the deck title, the `#`/`##` label headings in force, a table header over its rows, a spoil or tab label over its body — is a unit's `headings`, shown in the link review prompt (judged with the passage) and the knowledge review prompt of the content it heads; a link review is bound to the labels it was shown, and one recorded before round 5 (shown none) stands only while the labels equal the label baseline the first round-5 agent session logs.
requirements.source: 3C red team round 5 (studies/p11/redteam-r5/control and coherence, 2026-10-08) C3-01

requirements.statement: Visibility is decided at the attribute level (core/printed.mjs): a container's argument that orz copies into a style or attribute (`::: left <w>`, `::: cols <tracks>`, a `::: tab` label with a quote, markup in a `::: spoil` label) is checked against values known to show (a width/track of at least a readable size, a positive fr share, auto) and otherwise is content-hidden with its body unprinted; an argument the renderer drops is content-hidden; a block plugin's argument counts as printed only if the frame renders it as text ({{toc}}, {{smiles}}, {{youtube}} take a value — a level range, one SMILES string, a video id — anything else prints nothing; a chart line under an ignored key and a mermaid comment print nothing; an [argument] these plugins never read prints nothing); a slide's attributes, read from orz-slides' own parse, are allowlisted — any class, a background colour and fit=off hide the slide; a layout track giving a region under 8% of the slide or one the harness cannot size hides that region; a float off the slide, too small, behind it (z<0) or unplaceable is hidden, and a float (opaque) painted over a filled region, the title band, the footer or an earlier float hides what lies under it.
requirements.source: 3C red team round 6, CONTROL C1–C3 conformance (studies/p11/redteam-r6/control-c13, 2026-10-11) C1-01, C1-02, C1-03

requirements.statement: An included file is read under the includer's frame (core/shipped.mjs printedOnlyWhenIncluded): an include whose target, rendered as the includer's content, prints any line its own reading under its own frame leaves out (a deck's speaker notes or unrendered template lines printed as page text) is refused as include-unchecked, naming the first such line; an include of a document read under the same frame, or one that prints less there, is accepted.
requirements.source: 3C red team round 6, CONTROL C1–C3 conformance (studies/p11/redteam-r6/control-c13, 2026-10-11) C3-03

requirements.statement: Printed settings values are read in every frame: orz-paged's running header and footer values (header_left/center/right, footer_left/center/right of the first {{nyml kind: document}} block, multi-line values included) and the head metadata of a {{nyml kind: meta}} block (author, description; a label-sized title is a label shown with every unit, otherwise a unit) are framing units owing the off-plan read; an orz-paged setting that can hide the body (custom_css, a page background, a font size, line height or margin outside the readable range) is content-hidden; a document block in a page-frame file prints nothing and is no unit.
requirements.source: 3C red team round 6, CONTROL C1–C3 conformance (studies/p11/redteam-r6/control-c13, 2026-10-11) C3-02

requirements.statement: The one credit line that stays structure prints and credits the whole deliverable, so every unit of the deliverable carries it (`credit`), every link/framing review prompt and knowledge review prompt shows it with the labels, and a link review is bound to it (alignment.mjs reviewBasis); a review recorded before round 6 (shown no credit line) stands only while the deliverable's credit line equals the credit baseline the first round-6 agent session logs (a package with no credit baseline yet keeps its reviews), so an edited credit line voids every review of that deliverable and owes them again. While no current review of the deliverable has read its credit line, the first reviewable unit of it owes a framing review (framing-review-owed), whatever coverage needs.
requirements.source: 3C red team round 6, CONTROL C1–C3 conformance (studies/p11/redteam-r6/control-c13, 2026-10-11) C3-01

requirements.statement: What ships equals what is read (core/shipped.mjs): a shipped file is exempt only as a harness record named exactly — a list of known record files (the JSON records, metadata/ATTRIBUTION.md, alembic.json, LICENSE, CITATION.cff, .gitignore), record paths of known shapes (unit sidecars, verification dispatches, claim records, preflight receipts, spine origins and reviews, corrections) and the rights-evidence snapshots a record names — never by folder; every other markdown file must be a deliverable, the spine or a confirmed administrative document, and every other non-markdown file that can carry text (html, htm, txt, svg, json outside the records, any extension but image/audio/video/font media) is refused as document-unchecked wherever it ships from; the pack refuses both.
requirements.source: 3C red team round 6, CONTROL C1–C3 conformance (studies/p11/redteam-r6/control-c13, 2026-10-11) C3-04

requirements.statement: A figure (image, mermaid, chart, structure block) and the prose that names it — "the figure", "this diagram", "the image", "Figure N", a visual description or alt text — are linked both ways by `ref:` edges bound to the full wording: the figures of the prose's section, else the nearest figure before it; "Figure N" also the deliverable's Nth figure. A re-check owed through the edge is shown the figure as it is now.
requirements.source: 3C red team round 5 (studies/p11/redteam-r5/control and coherence, 2026-10-08) coherence F1

requirements.statement: A multi-word key term is also used by its distinctive word alone: a modifier of its label or alias (every word but the head noun, four letters or more, not a function word) that no other key term's label or alias shares ("exothermic" for "exothermic reaction"; never "reaction" or "equilibrium"), within the chapter that defines it and any chapter that uses the term by its full name; such a unit carries the term edge, baselined like any key-term edge, and owes a re-check when the term is redefined.
requirements.source: 3C red team round 5 (studies/p11/redteam-r5/control and coherence, 2026-10-08) coherence F6

requirements.statement: Ownership follows the text, never the unit id (R5-K09, R5-K10): a unit holding words the instructor wrote — its own record, the record of any unit whose text it holds (lineage: a split, a merge, a piece or near return of a retired unit, a neighbour or new unit that took in a retired unit's words, in any form or deliverable; the retired-unit register), or the instructor's logged authorship confirmation of either — is the instructor's. Every authorship consumer asks this one rule (core/authorship.mjs): the correction guard's two-source rule, D35 acceptance, instructor-edit-unasked, claim keys and asked changes, assessment fidelity. The unit index mints the same credit into the new record (with the agent's revision on record), and no unit-record write may take the credit or drop the lineage.

A setting that changes what is checked is bound to the decision log (R5 F2): once the log shows spine v2 in force, a lowered, missing or unreadable spine setting in metadata/coursewerk.json is a blocking defect (setting-lowered) and the v2 core runs regardless; a package registry may demote a standard module only by the instructor's logged module-change decision (else unlogged-demotion, run at standard maturity); retrieval destinations and the digest size are read from the instructor's logged acts, never the file.

A self-written mark decides nothing (R5 F3): a unit record's new or changed version carry counts only through the instructor's logged units-carried record naming the unit after its record was last written, and a carry clears nothing a unit owed — what it owed is kept, so its re-check is shown what moved; a correction counts as shown only when the log shows it shown; a link counts as resolved only as the log records the resolution.

A chapter scope is decided by content, never by a file name (R5 F4): a new major version carries the chapter's own deliverables, every unit linked to one of the chapter's spine nodes, every unit of a declared document that declares the chapter, and (fail-safe) every unit of a declared document linked to no chapter's node; the restated-objective check and MS7's value scope read a declared document's chapter from what it declares and links.
